overview: The School Committee discussed transitions from remote to full in-person learning, received updates on COVID-19 health protocols and the budget, and planned year-end senior activities. The committee also approved a solar panel lease agreement for Andrews Middle School and adopted resolutions regarding student representatives and after-school equity.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee voted to enter executive session to prepare for contract negotiations with the superintendent before returning to open session.

items.title: Decorum and Rules of Order
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn and Member McLaughlin reiterated expectations for civil discourse, stating that insults will result in speakers being muted and emphasizing that remarks must be directed through the chair.

items.title: Routine Business: Minutes, Financial Approvals, and Subcommittees
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from March 8, regular payrolls and accounts, and subcommittee reports for Buildings and Grounds, Personnel and Budget, and Special Education/Behavioral Health, while tabling Curriculum and Committee of the Whole reports.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Community members submitted communications and spoke on issues including the Columbus School renaming committee application, deep concerns regarding potential teacher changes for remote students, and capacity challenges in the before- and after-school program.

items.title: Superintendent's Updates
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent denounced anti-Asian hate, updated the public on the Columbus School renaming process, and discussed the district's phase-in plan for full in-person elementary learning by April 5 in response to DESE mandates.

items.title: COVID-19 Health and Testing Update
items.summary: Health Services Supervisor Toni Wray reported an uptick in Medford's COVID-19 incidence rate, provided school pooled testing statistics, and outlined new state guidance regarding three-foot distancing and vaccine rollout schedules.

items.title: FY21 and FY22 Budget Update
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent David Murphy presented an overview of the FY21 budget closeout, addressing revolving account deficits in food services and exploring how pending federal ESSER funds might be strategically deployed across multiple years.

items.title: Summer Programming
items.summary: District administrators reported on plans for summer school, the Vocational School's Summer Discovery Program, and general remediation, while the committee voted to place a dedicated Summer Fun program update on the April 12 agenda.

items.title: Class of 2021 Senior Activities
items.summary: Administrators and committee members discussed tentative end-of-year events for seniors, including an outdoor graduation at Hormel Stadium on June 2 and plans to coordinate prom logistics under outdoor gathering limits.

items.title: Andrews Middle School Solar Panel Lease
items.summary: Approved a resolution permitting the city to lease rooftop and parking lot space at Andrews Middle School to a third party to install, operate, and maintain solar panels and carport solar canopies.

items.title: Resolutions on Student Representatives and After-School Equity
items.summary: Approved a resolution scheduling a discussion on integrating student representative voices, as well as a resolution requiring demographic data collection on before- and after-school applicants to assess and improve equity.
